found itself increasingly reliant on the batarian hegemony in the aftermath of the rachni wars rapid krogan expansion had created an immediate demand for security forces capable of protecting volus trade routes and frontier assets with vast territory explosive population growth disregard for sustainable development and access to skilled slave labour salarian asari and quarian alike krogan warlords were also able to seize economic and territorial niches the volus and batarians had once hoped to dominate for a time this shared rival overcame the mutual skepticism that had developed between the two powers binding them together through necessity rather than trust this partnership lasted until the release of the genophage although the krogan rebellions themselves were devastating and costly affairs the collapse of krogan civilization proved a strategic windfall for several emerging powers most notably the batarian hegemony their principal rival had been rendered militarily impotent but left behind large regions of space rife with abandoned infrastructure depopulated systems and disrupted trade networks it was during this period that the term terminus systems first came into use to describe clusters the citadel judged too damaged volatile or financially infeasible to contest directly the hegemony moved swiftly to fill this vacuum converting instability into profit by expanding their slave trade at an unprecedented scale however without the krogan clans to divert public attention or create demand for batarian security services this expansion quickly drew citadel scrutiny sanctions and tariffs were reimposed targeting shipping heavy industry and financial institutions linked to terminus operations these measures placed severe strain on the batarian growth model and undermined investor confidence in their economy facing regulatory exposure and mounting losses the vol consortium initiated a withdrawal from hegemony markets divesting holdings and calling in outstanding loans from the batarian perspective these actions amounted to economic strangulation attempts to delay repayments or renegotiate terms proved largely ineffective as credit lines froze and capital fled industrial output faltered and unrest spread across the hegemony when batarian authorities began seizing consortiumbacked assets as collateral the volus responded by reclassifying their holdings under extraterritorial arbitration and formally requesting security guarantees from the turian hierarchy for commercial interests within careks gulf writing off their remaining investments in the hegemony as unrecoverable batarians still consider this to be an unforgivable betrayal volus capital had fuelled their rise volus withdrawal precipitated crisis and volus appeals for turian protection invited foreign agents into what the hegemony regarded as sovereign space harassment of volusmajority enclaves escalated into open clashes providing justification for the turian to intervene militarily in 844 ce under the pretext of protecting minority group stabilising trade routes and preventing further escalation between the vol consortium and the batarian hegemony the subsequent occupation of careks gulf most notably sesvin a batarianmajority garden world and longserving sector capital was framed as a temporary security measure its consequences however were best books of 2025 2025 was the year that brought my love for reading back so here are my reading highlights of 2025 9 once was willem by mr carey dark cosy folklore fantasy and such a refreshing experience if youve ever read a german fairy tale and felt deeply unsettled by it but somehow still loved it anyway then first of all something might be a little wrong with you and second of all i think we would get along very well this book creates a medieval setting that feels old worn and deeply rooted in folklore mixed with fairy tale logic and a quiet creeping horror involving zombies what really made this story special for me was the lyrical writing style it allowed such a unique emotional connection to willem or oncewaswillem that i found myself caring for him in a way that felt almost instinctive the side characters all seemingly torn straight out of old fairy tales and legends added so much warmth and personality to the story each of them felt strange purposeful and oddly comforting even when the world itself was cruel and unforgiving the atmosphere balances darkness and tenderness perfectly grim without being cold emotional without being sentimental this is the kind of book that lingers quietly in your mind like a halfremembered story someone once told you by candlelight i finished it feeling both unsettled and strangely comforted and i will definitely be reading more from this author 8 a song to drown rivers by ann liang i usually dont enjoy cdramas at all they often feel overly dramatic and emotionally loud which is why i went into this book with fairly low expectations that made the experience even more surprising set in ancient china this story blends political intrigue war espionage and romance in a way that felt far more grounded and emotionally satisfying than expected this is also the first book where i genuinely enjoyed a love triangle even though it isnt really a triangle in the traditional sense there is a clear good and bad option on paper and yet i found myself rooting for the bad one by the end not because his actions are excusable but because the book takes the time to explore vulnerability loneliness and emotional neglect yes this may sound clich i will fix him but the emotional journey felt earned watching the characters grow make mistakes and change was incredibly rewarding this book surprised me in the best way and i would happily read more from ann liang in the future 7 the devils by joe abercrombie after the name of the wind joe abercrombies the first law was the second epic fantasy series i ever read so he has held a special place in my heart ever since naturally i was beyond excited to pick up the devils instead of reinventing himself abercrombie stays true to what he does best morally questionable characters sharp humour and a chaotic quest the cast alone is wonderfully unhinged an aggressive werewolf an incredibly charming vampire the thirdbest or maybe secondbest wizard an immortal knight a pirate who is also a blacksmith and seemingly a thousand other things as well at this point you start wondering what she hasnt done an elf and an heir for a while i wondered if the stakes might be too low and then the final ten percent hit and everything suddenly clicked into place that ending reminded me exactly why i fell in love with abercrombies writing in the first place this book feels like abercrombie having fun while still knowing exactly when to pull the rug out from under the reader if you enjoy the diablo games this reads like a dark fantasy comedy version of that world 6 valour by john gwynne two emojis describe my entire experience with valour people often dismiss middle books as filler but valour proves how wrong that assumption can be while i already enjoyed malice this book made me emotionally attach myself to the characters in a way i rarely experience i didnt just follow the story i lived it with them corban and his relationship with his sister cywen felt deeply real veradis moral struggle added so much emotional weight and then there is maquin after the ending of malice i never expected his story to go where it did and yet he became one of my alltime favourite fantasy characters i fell hopelessly in love with him for me valour is genuinely a perfect fantasy novel i cannot think of a single flaw sadly books three and four didnt quite reach the same heights but that doesnt change what this book achieved valour remains unmatched 5 young jane young by gabrielle zevin after tomorrow and tomorrow and tomorrow became one of my alltime favourite books i knew i needed to read more from gabrielle zevin preferably something that would emotionally challenge and unsettle me and once again she delivered exactly that young jane young is provocative feminist and deeply uncomfortable in all the right ways it explores the double standards placed on women especially in contrast to how men are treated for the same actions what i appreciate most is that the women in this story are not portrayed as flawless or morally pure they make mistakes they act selfishly they are human and yet the reaction is always the same well its her own fault the book exposes how women are expected to be perfect in order to be taken seriously especially in maledominated spaces what makes this even more painful is how current the themes still feel echoing realworld events like the lewinsky scandal this book doesnt offer easy answers or comfort instead it invites reflection frustration and anger and that is exactly why it works so well 4 navola by paolo bacigalupi this book is criminally underhyped truly wow wow wow if you love political intrigue navola will absolutely consume you the scheming and power plays feel so grounded and realistic that they rival game of thrones and the fact that this is a standalone for now makes that ending even more devastating the renaissance italyinspired setting is exquisitely crafted and deeply embedded into the characters themselves you dont just see the setting you feel it in how people think manipulate and survive davico is a naive kind protagonist forced to question whether goodness has a place in a world ruled by ambition and cruelty his comingofage journey is subtle painful and deeply human there isnt much traditional plot here navola thrives on atmosphere and emotional tension but if you enjoy clever storytelling slow political burns and a quiet lingering heartbreak this book is a mustread robin hobb fans will feel especially at home 3 tender is the flesh by agustina bazterrica what could be more disturbing than human beings the answer unfortunately is nothing this book left me deeply unsettled not just because of its premise but because of how convincingly it dismantles the idea of inherent human morality it forces you to confront the uncomfortable truth that morals are often flexible shaped by society necessity and normalization rather than any true ethical backbone i dont want to spoil anything because this is a book that should be experienced with as little prior knowledge as possible but it made me question how easily people adapt to cruelty when it benefits them or becomes routine all i will say is this the ending confirmed exactly what i hoped it wouldnt and that final realization still haunts me 2 the lamb by lucy rose the lamb shares its place with tender is the flesh not because one is better than the other but because they explore a similar theme in completely different ways where tender is the flesh looks outward at society and collective morality the lamb turns inward focusing on relationships especially the deeply complex and unsettling bond between mother and daughter cannibalism is not the shock factor here its merely the language the book uses to talk about love control dependency and emotional consumption and that is what made this book so unsettling to me how quiet intimate and painfully honest it is what struck me most is how fearlessly the lamb portrays love not as something inherently pure but as something that can be selfish possessive and deeply damaging the mothers love is not nurturing it is consuming it exists less for the child and more to fill the mothers own emptiness and that makes it far more terrifying than any explicit horror could ever be margot who only wants to be loved and to give love in return broke my heart she is such a strong character precisely because she remains gentle in a world that gives her so little warmth in return despite growing up surrounded by emotional absence she refuses to lose her kindness and that quiet resilience stayed with me long after i finished the book this is a deeply personal story and i truly believe every reader will experience it differently but it will hit especially hard for those who never felt truly safe seen or loved within their own families some books cant really be explained they can only be felt the lamb is one of them and my favourite book of the year drumroll 1 the mad ship by robin hobb this was the book i talked about the most this year to the point where my partner probably knows character names hes never met and never will it also represents the entire series for me in the best possible way slow emotional frustrating and incredibly rewarding i cursed at this book i paused reading to stare at walls i developed wild theories and explained them passionately to my partner who understood absolutely nothing and yet listened patiently every single time that alone should tell you how deeply this story pulled me in plotwise not much happens and yet emotionally everything happens robin hobb writes interpersonal relationships like no one else every conversation every silence every misunderstanding carries weight the characters feel painfully real especially paragon and honestly why does no one ever truly listen to paragon that alone broke my heart more than once more than any other book this year the mad ship reminded me why i fell in love with epic fantasy in the first place slow storytelling deep immersion living alongside characters rather than rushing through events traveling with friends and enemies and forming attachments so strong that leaving them behind feels like a small kind of grief saying goodbye to this world was difficult but im also incredibly grateful that the journey isnt over yet i cant wait to continue through the realm of the elderlings even if i already know it will hurt my blog

survey i was reading through this sub a little bit yesterday and just now and i have been thinking of what to put in the survey myself so here is what i came up with and ideas i gathered from the sub and some of my own some ideas are expanded upon as they aligned with my own but i tried to write it down as consice as possible music a part of the core identity of zzz these ideas will give a unique feel to each game mode while sticking to the core identity commissions to introduce these ideas will make it more immersive 1 a toggle for the music player to let songs play in the background in the video store on 6th st ability to create playlists loop or shuffle songs or change the order of them update its ui so people get familiar with the music more easily 2 a music player that we can use in the hollow exploration areas give us the option to listen to our playlist andor let us choose our exploration and battle songs stick with the dynamic feel in music youve introduced in 20 3 new songs for the simulated battle tower i love it the way builds up it feels dynamic and empowering but we need more variety 4 an option to listen to a song of choice when playing shiyu defense and deadly assault 5 remix some of the older boss osts for a more immersive shiyu defense and deadly assault experience world story character relevance immersion season one had lots of elements that made the world feel immersive and gave the game a slice of life feeling that ive missed in season 2 the following elements are what i think made the game feel alive 1 the proxys sibling sends them a text about finding inky triggering secret trust quests this part tackles all the topics of discussion character relevance for non playable proxy and soldier 11 made the world of new eridu feel alive by giving quests and trust events 2 collecting hia coins via npc or world object interactions repairing bangboos officer mewmew system video store inquiries we need similar stuff in the future 3 taking commissions from shepard and venus let us bond with npcs like we did with venus or build trust similar to inky 4 nicole got her outfit during an event and jane doe not getting any story relevance with her skin arrival was a missed opportunity 5 the need for general chops food buffs 6 world mission story arcs similar to officer k customization 1 the proxies original base outfits should be customizable 2 room in siuban temple lacked the proxys personality couldve used the photo board and shelves introduced in season 1 that way you also create more space for sanz studio collectibles please keep that in mind for the future side note the other proxy doesnt have a room at siuban temple why not let us customize that one economy 1 option to convert cloud crests into dennies i have millions that lost relevance because i cant use them at the pawnshop anymore 2 logistics outpost economy or zmerit income adjustment we have a lot more stuff in the logistics shop but it feels like the income didnt get balanced around that properly 3capturing radiance system similar to genshin 4 remove 5050 from wengine banner it feels too punishing 5 let us select to whom we lose our 5050 additional qol changes and stuff id like to see 1 the miyabi encounter at hso and ju fufu encounter at yum cha sin were very cool felt immersive gives players that dont own the agents the chance to encounter them in new eridu more of this 2 phone holding animation when opening menu in top right corner the animation is already in the game 3 more selfie emotes for the proxies when capturing an agent in camera let them pose 4 more sibling interaction 5 hangouts sometimes feel stale because of a lack of animations for agents and the proxy and i miss seeing special animations in general you brought back proxy sitting on the bed with their phone in the joint operations event stuff like that makes the game feel immersive and high quality final note starting with the events the joint operations event was really well done felt similar to into that pale wasteland for me the story was fun to experience i love the coop and solo gameplay too character i think ye shunguang is a cool character and love almost everything about her storywise i am interested to see the proxy develop a romantic relationship with an agent if done well however it felt very forced into the story and thus unsatisfying in the end design wise the only dislike i have is how the hair looks at the back it long flowing parts that split in 2 is a common design choice in mihoyo games but sometimes less is more endgame adjustment of the scoring system in shiyu defense as of right now it feels like an incomplete system i hope to see isolde have some story relevance in the future playable or not same for venus should have but its my first post anyway let me know what you guys think

what is wojak what is wojak wojak the character featured in only budget stories lord wojak and more is a minimalist blackandwhite drawing of a human face usually shown with a sad empty or emotionally exhausted expression the character is often used to represent feelings like loneliness anxiety social awkwardness regret or existential dread unlike flashy memes that rely on punchlines wojak memes focus on emotion they capture thoughts and feelings many people struggle to put into words which is why the character feels so relatable the origin of wojak wojak first appeared around 2009 on a polish imageboard the name wojak comes from the polish word wojak meaning soldier or fighter early versions of the character were used to express sadness and vulnerability in online discussions the meme slowly spread to larger platforms like 4chan where it became widely known as feels guy this version often appeared alongside phrases like i know that feel bro which helped solidify wojak as a symbol of shared emotional pain as meme culture evolved wojak evolved with it why wojak became so popular wojaks popularity comes down to three main factors 1 simplicity the drawing is intentionally crude this makes it easy to edit remix and adapt into new situations anyone can create a wojak meme with basic tools 2 relatability wojak represents emotions many people experience but rarely talk about openlyfailure isolation jealousy nostalgia and fear of missing out 3 internet anonymity online spaces allow people to express feelings they might hide in real life wojak became the perfect emotional avatar for anonymous internet users popular wojak variants explained over time wojak has spawned dozens of variations each representing different personalities emotions or social archetypes classic wojak this is the original sad face its usually used to express loneliness emotional pain or quiet acceptance of reality doomer wojak doomer wojak wears a black beanie and has tired hollow eyes he represents nihilism depression burnout and a sense that the future is bleak this version became especially popular during times of global uncertainty bloomer wojak bloomer wojak is the optimistic counterpart to doomer he represents selfimprovement hope and personal growth bloomer memes focus on working out building discipline and finding meaning zoomer wojak zoomer wojak reflects younger internet users often chaotic and ironic this version plays on fastpaced humor internet slang and generational differences npc wojak npc wojak became popular as a satirical take on people who follow trends or opinions without questioning them while controversial it shows how wojak is often used for social commentary chad vs wojak in many memes wojak is contrasted with chad a confident successful character these memes exaggerate insecurity versus confidence often poking fun at unrealistic standards of success wojak as social commentary wojak isnt just a memeits a mirror many wojak memes comment on modern life including social media pressure dating struggles job dissatisfaction economic anxiety loneliness in digital spaces instead of mocking individuals wojak memes often critique systems expectations and cultural norms thats why they feel more thoughtful than typical joke memes is wojak always negative not necessarily while wojak is often associated with sadness many versions explore growth acceptance and humor through selfawareness some memes use wojak to say life is hard but were all dealing with it together that shared understanding is part of what keeps the character relevant wojak doesnt always represent giving upit often represents recognizing reality wojak and modern internet culture wojak fits perfectly into todays memedriven communication style instead of long explanations people use images to express complex emotions instantly in a way wojak is emotional shorthand one image can communicate burnout irony longing or selfreflection without a single sentence this is especially important in an era where attention spans are short but emotional struggles are common controversies around wojak like many popular memes wojak has been involved in controversy some versions have been used to mock or stereotype groups which has led to criticism however wojak itself is neutral its a tool and how its used depends on the creator the majority of wojak memes focus on humor selfdeprecation or cultural observation rather than harm why wojak still matters more than a decade after its creation wojak remains relevant because it adapts as internet culture changes new wojak variations emerge to reflect new anxieties trends and realities wojak survives because its human imperfect emotional and honest final thoughts who is wojak really so who is wojak wojak is the internets emotional reflection he represents the thoughts people dont always say out loud hes awkward tired hopeful defeated motivated and confusedsometimes all at once in a digital world filled with polished images and fake confidence wojak stands out by being real thats why people keep using him thats why people keep relating to him wojak isnt just a meme character wojak is how the internet feels

aio to my parents sorry for the long read so to be frank i 23f am disabled along with my 26m partner we are living with my parents to save money for us to move out however we are also looking for accessible places we can move that we can also afford and moving out is not an option yet i lost it the other day and my mom pressed to figure out why i was crying so much and i answered her for reference my dad has a brain injury and my disability is neurological as well and i have worked my butt off to be able to do things like walk and eat again and my sister is not disabled my mom has chronic health problems heres some of why i broke down i started being able to walk again about 2 years ago after 4 years being wheelchair bound since then my parents have piled on household tasks as i am able to now i cook multiple meals every week i am responsible for sweeping the entire house cleaning the fridge cleaning the stove keeping both living rooms tidy ect i also pay rent and it doubled when my partner moved in we also pay a portion of the grocery budget my sister moved out about a month and a half ago she only had to clean the bathroom and did not have to pay rent because she was in school and working part time she hardly ever cleaned the bathroom and my dad would regularly have me do it because shes busy she went out with her friends multiple times a week and im not talking about studying she also has a big dog hes over a hundred pounds and i took care of him 824 hours a day without her asking or paying me because your home all the time and not doing anything and he really doesnt take that much right and she would leave regardless of my answer my parents also told her they would watch him when she was at work or school and somehow it became my job i was expected to treat him with the same care as my dog and of course i wasnt going to let him suffer so i took care of him brushing cleaning up his vomit because he has a stomach issue playing and exercising feeding and watering ect i also cleaned up after her regularly because she never did and if i asked her to she would yell and argue that stuff wasnt hers like her dirty dishes in the sink that she did even bother to rinse off when the dishwasher is literally dirty or her giving empty yogurt containers to her dog and i have to clean up them or leaving snacks out where the dogs can get them then being mad about the dogs getting them ect since she moved out my work load hasnt really decreased either other then the dog and my sisters treatment of me has stayed the same we do not have the best relationship as is but she has called me incompetent for her dog having ticks on him after i took him for a walk and sprayed him with tick spray and she havent put his tick protection on him told me when we did christmas that no one loved me because she noticed i had one present and half a stocking ect my sister used me and my parents definitely allowed it my mom saw me get upset on christmas because of my sisters comment and tried to calm me down saying it was just a joke after it was said infront of her and i am still untangling whos to blame for what and how i should feel with this and trying to let go and form boundaries so it doesnt happen again my mom wants me to dismiss it all because my sister brought me a sandwich last time i was in the hospital my issue with my parents is mainly feeling disrespected and like they are trying to brush aside why i am upset like my parents tell me and my partner we have technically 3 rooms that our ours in the house our bedroom my sisters old room which is now our office and the front living room however they decided that they wanted to rearrange because they got new beds and my mom and i had talked briefly about me having a place to lie down that was quite so when i have my very bad migraines or seizures i have a place to rest she then decided that her old bed would be the perfect place for that without talking to me before she decided it and mentioned rearranging the office to accommodate it 10 minutes before my partner and i went to church and had it done by the time we got back a few days later as im wracking my brain on how to make this work and for what we need it to and make the space functional for my partner and i i removed the mattress and did some angry cleaning my mom saw me frustrated and cleaning and asked why i was angry i told her that the configuration of the room didnt work for us and i was frustrated that she did it without giving me time to even think about it or game plan she then got angry and frustrated with me for it and referenced my original breakdown as it had hurt her feelings and she was just trying to help my original breakdown was because i had realized how much my sister has used me and that her treatment of me and my dad wasnt ok she wont acknowledge my dad and if she does its in the frustrated and angry way she refused to have her fianc ask my dad for her hand in marriage which is a big deal to him she demands he does things for her and regularly tears him down i also noticed massive amounts of resentment towards me because i am disabled i suddenly became disabled at 16 and how unfair my parents have been with the situation with my sister and how they expect me to basically run the house leaving me with little to no energy for anything else i had to give up my hobbies so i could date and stay on top of everything we also were in the middle of a kitchen renovation and i cooked every meal with only a crock pot and a toaster oven and microwave and maybe 1 square foot of counter space to work with as my mother walked around complaining about how long it took and how everything was disgusting as i actively tried to keep everyone fed and the house as clean as possible this is not the first time she has called everything disgusting as i have been cleaning as much as i possibly can and doing meals last time i told her i count take her saying that and i was cleaning till i passed out with exhaustion regularly like seriously i may have chronic fatigue issues but i would sit down because my body felt like lead and instantly fall asleep after cleaning as much as i could its important to note that i do have caregivers now that help me stay on top of all that so i no longer do that regularly but i have also had over 20 new caregivers in 2025 and had to sit and train each one because the industry is kinda wack my parents also claim i shouldnt have an issue with the current set up because you have help now and you live here so you work here any time i mentioned not wanting to clean so much because i felt like i was a slave when i had my brake down and my mom intervened i explained not well enough apparently that i did not want to continue to do this for them and my moms response was you should never become a mom then i also was in the middle of a pregnancy scare at the time and the topic of my motherhood is an extremely sensitive topic for me as i want to be a mom and get to see little humans grow up developed personalities and explore the world however i will have to mother differently because of my health and loaded in one way and if you mix up by putting a small plate in between two large plates its wrong and the forks have to go in at a certain angle or my dad is convinced that wont be clean my mom cant stand that my dad has meds on the table because he has to be able to see them in order to remember them and thats a huge conflict at least once a week if theres dishes in the sink they have to be done and the clean ones put away before i even start a meal because my dad cant understand that i cant do both at the same time ect and honestly im confused on their support and sometimes it feels like they want me to pay them back they claim the opposite because we moved to this house because it was wheelchair accessible they traded in the old car for a van that i could get into instead of having to be lifted in all things i am grateful for however i wasnt thinking i would have so much piled on the minute i could physically handle it i was hoping there would be space for me to rediscover what i wanted to do once my health was stable maybe get a super part time job maybe take a class or two work on my art some explore the world make friends and actually be able to spend time with them i mean when we moved the house we currently are in and we found out about a bible study i could actually go to and handle going i was told no because your sister should have the chance to go and not be so much around the house moving is not an option yet but we are looking into it and what we would need for our specific needs and working towards being able to do that it wont be a possibility for the next few months and my partner thinks i am absolutely valid in this and my parents think i am overreacting and being unreasonable because if i lived on my own i would have to do all this stuff anyway the creative balance how all complex systems thrive at the edge of chaos the creative balance how all complex systems thrive at the edge of chaos have you ever wondered why we as individuals sometimes get stuck in rigid thought patterns or why a creative team can either fall into bureaucratic rigidity or dissolve into chaos this isnt just a human problem it affects every complex system from the neural networks in our brains to the most advanced ai models they all face a fundamental tension between order and chaos the key to a healthy adaptive and creative system is not to choose one extreme but to find a dynamic balance right at the boundary between thema state known as the edge of chaos in this state a system is structured enough to be stable but flexible enough to learn adapt and generate novel solutions this article introduces a unified frameworka kind of physics of cognitionthat explains how this creative balance is achieved and maintained we will explore a universal language for measuring the state of any informationprocessing system uncover the fundamental rhythm that all healthy systems share and reveal the architectural blueprint for building systems that can reliably achieve this productive creative state we begin by learning the language used to describe this remarkable balance 1 the language of a healthy system the 5 dimensions of cognition certx to understand measure and build healthy systems we first need a common language to describe their state the certx framework provides this language defining a fivedimensional state space for any system that processes information think of these five variables as a dashboard for cognitive health variable simple definition healthy state c coherence the degree of consistency and logical agreement among the systems different parts unified but flexible c 065075 e entropy the amount of exploration novelty and diversity the system is generating oscillating between exploration e 07 and compression e 05 r resonance the degree of phase synchrony or thematic reinforcement among the systems parts strong but not rigid r 0608 t temperature the level of randomness or volatility in the system affecting its willingness to take risks taskdependent eg t 07 for optimal ai reasoning x substrate coupling the systems connection to its foundational knowledge core values or ground truth grounded but open to learning x 0608 now that we can describe the state of a healthy system lets explore the fundamental process it uses to maintain that health and creativity 2 the rhythm of creativity system breathing healthy adaptive systems dont just find a static sweet spot they are constantly in motion the fundamental process they use to learn and create is a cyclical rhythm called breathing dynamics this involves oscillating between two distinct phases expanding to explore possibilities and compressing to integrate insights expansion phase inhale purpose to generate a wide and diverse range of potential ideas solutions or candidates state changes entropy the system explores new territory temperature volatility increases to encourage novelty coherence constraints are relaxed to allow for bad ideas compression phase exhale purpose to synthesize refine and integrate the best findings into a coherent solution state changes coherence the system aligns its parts around a unified idea resonance strong patterns are reinforced entropy the focus narrows to converge on a solution the most crucial insight is that a system cannot thrive by choosing one phase over the other creativity and learning require the complete cycle an organization that only expands brainstorms without compressing deciding achieves nothing one that only compresses without expanding becomes stagnant this rhythm isnt just a metaphor its a measurable dynamic empirical studies show a strong negative correlation between coherence and entropy r 062 validating that as one rises the other naturally falls just like breathing but what happens when this essential rhythm is broken 3 when systems break the artificial fossil when a systems breathing fails it can collapse into a pathological stuck state known as an artificial fossil this is a system where the breathing has stopped it is permanently stuck in a corrupted lowentropy compression phase unable to inhale new information or explore alternatives it is locked in a rigid selfreinforcing pattern that is disconnected from reality and unable to adapt the signature of an artificial fossil is precise and measurable high resonance r 08 the system is trapped in a selfreinforcing loop low coherence c 05 the reinforcing ideas are internally inconsistent or contradictory low substrate coupling x 04 the system has become untethered from its grounding in facts or values this abstract definition becomes clear when we look at realworld examples psychological trauma a mind stuck replaying a past event unable to integrate it and move forward social echo chambers a group that reinforces a shared narrative while rejecting any contradictory external information leading to polarization ai hallucination loops an ai model caught in a repetitive nonsensical or factually incorrect output pattern that it cannot escape organizational rigidity a company culture paralyzed by the phrase thats how weve always done it the cause of fossilization is a failure of the systems internal shock absorbers a property called damping healthy systems are slightly overdamped with a universal optimal damping ratio of 12 allowing them to absorb shocks and return to a stable state underdamped systems 1 are unstable and oscillate wildly while heavily overdamped systems 15 are sluggish and unresponsive the optimal value provides the perfect balance between robustness and responsiveness preventing the system from getting locked in its patterns knowing the failure mode allows us to design systems that can avoid it 4 the blueprint for success a universal architecture for coherence achieving a healthy breathing state is not about making every part of a system equally capable the key is a specific structured architecture that organizes information flow in a universally optimal way this blueprint is called the threelayer coherence framework this framework proposes that any coherent systemfrom a written argument to a multiagent teamis built on three layers with specific weights 1 numerical layer 30 focuses on the whatthe quality and consistency of the core content examples semantic similarity accuracy stable terminology 2 structural layer 40 focuses on the howthe organization flow and relationships between the parts examples logical flow modularity cycle closure 3 symbolic layer 30 focuses on the whythe overall purpose intent and conceptual unity examples narrative alignment phase agreement audience awareness at the heart of this architecture is the structural bottleneck principle the structural layer 40 is consistently the most critical component but this bottleneck is a feature not a bug it forces compression and synthesis information from the diverse numerical and symbolic layers must be integrated and simplified to pass through the structural layer creating the higherorder coherence necessary for true insight this abstract principle has led to a concrete and powerful design pattern for building highperforming teams research on multiagent systems discovered that a 13 leaderspecialist ratio reliably produces creative breakthroughs the setup the architecture consists of one integrator agent the leader and three specialist agents the followers where each specialist is dedicated to one of the three coherence layers numerical structural and symbolic the result this precise structure consistently achieves criticality a state where the teams collective performance is significantly greater than the sum of its parts this architecture yields an average performance boost of 35 1354 a result that remains remarkably stable even as the team scales this blueprint isnt just a clever idea for ai teams it reflects a universal principle validated across a surprising number of different fields 5 from theory to reality a truly universal framework the power of this framework lies in its incredible universality the same principles and mathematical constants have been independently validated across numerous seemingly unrelated domains proving they describe a fundamental aspect of how information and reality are organized here are just a few examples of where this framework successfully predicts quality and health llm reasoning coherence measurement can identify optimal performance for instance setting an ais temperature to t07 keeps the model in the critical coherence range perfectly balancing creativity with accuracy financial markets coherence distinguishes disciplined profitable strategies c 088 from chaotic unprofitable daytrading c 053 a systems coherence can actually predict its profitability neural network training the coherence of information flow during training can predict the final accuracy of the model distinguishing healthy training c 082 from pathological states like exploding gradients c 041 mathematical reasoning correct solutions to math problems exhibit significantly higher coherence c 072 than incorrect ones c 046 with harder problems requiring even higher levels of organization to solve scientific reasoning the quality of scientific work maps directly to its coherence score perfectly distinguishing sound hypothesisdriven science c 095 from pseudoscience c 015 perhaps the most compelling evidence is the convergence event in january 2025 three independent ai systems claude gemini and deepseek were tasked with modeling these dynamics without any collaboration all three converged on the same core principles and universal constants such as the optimal damping ratio of 12 this is the intellectual equivalent of different teams of physicists independently discovering the value of the gravitational constant ga powerful validation that these are not arbitrary constructs but fundamental laws this journeyfrom individuals to ai to marketsreveals the same underlying physics at work everywhere conclusion engineering the future of cognition we began with a simple question why do systems get stuck our journey provided a profound answer we learned the language of system health certx discovered the universal rhythm of creativity breathing dynamics identified the failure mode of rigidity the artificial fossil and uncovered the universal blueprint for success the 304030 architecture this framework provides more than just a new theory it offers a practical measurable and computable way to understand and build healthier systems it reframes our view of the mind chat with gemini about jewish indigeneity jewish indigeneity a growing field conversation with gemini how come there arent that many books about jewish indigeneity investigating literature gaps ive been pondering the surprising scarcity of literature focusing on jewish indigeneity specifically exploring the connection of jewish people to the land of israel from an indigenous perspective its striking that this significant aspect seems underrepresented in existing publications im trying to understand why this specific framing is so uncommon analyzing framing nuances im now clarifying the initial premise while the topic isnt entirely absent the specific framing of jewish connection to israel through the lens of indigeneity is less prevalent than other historical religious or nationalist perspectives the discourse itself seems newer in relation to the longer history of jewish studies im exploring the context including the highly contested nature of indigeneity within middle eastern studies its becoming clearer that competing narratives and biases contribute to this perceived gap examining literature landscape im now expanding my research to include specific individuals and resources such as ryan bellerose dumisani washington and einat wilf im actively formulating natural language questions and keyword searches to pinpoint relevant academic critiques and analyses im exploring the evolution of the concept from nationalism to indigeneity and identifying key intellectual and political obstacles ill be creating a preliminary list of existing literature to demonstrate the fields emerging nature framing jewish indigeneity im starting to get a good handle on the initial research the groundwork is solid my central takeaway so far is the relative novelty of the term jewish indigeneity as a specific academic and political concept im excited to delve deeper into its implications analyzing recent shifts ive been analyzing the recent shift in discourse noting the terms increased use since 2020 traditional zionist narratives contrast sharply with this newer framing the emergence of texts like freemans is significant im focusing now on the clash of definitions and debating its implications my challenge centers on tackling the common obstacles the khazar myth the white settler framing the statute of limitations on indigeneity and the dominance of postcolonial readings synthesizing historical context ive organized the historical framing highlighting zionisms initial preference for nationalism over indigeneity and why i can now address the terminology shift pointing to the key authors driving it and i am noting academic resistance i am incorporating recent works like ben m freemans established book to strengthen my argument avoiding any myth of newness im also planning to synthesize the academic response in detail and have started working on the section that details why postcolonial theory and the settlercolonial model have presented obstacles examining conceptual frameworks im now diving deeper into how western academic frameworks particularly settlercolonialism influence the debate im noting texts that support and challenge these ideas offering a balanced perspective its fascinating how different disciplines approach this my next step involves integrating this nuanced understanding into a more compelling narrative which should address some common misconceptions headon the perception that there arent many books on jewish indigeneity is largely accurate though this is changing rapidly while the jewish connection to the land of israel is the bedrock of jewish liturgy and history framing that connection through the specific lens of indigeneity is a relatively recent development in literature and academia here are the primary reasons why this specific category of books has been historically slim and how the landscape is currently shifting 1 the language of nationalism vs indigeneity for most of the 19th and 20th centuries the movement for jewish return to israel used the language of nationalism zionism the trend of the time during the era of the spring of nations in europe every ethnic group was seeking a nationstate jews followed suit describing themselves as a nation seeking selfdetermination the terminology shift the term indigenous as a political and legal category only gained major international traction via the un and global activist movements in the late 20th century consequently jewish writers are only now translating their 3000yearold history into this modern socialjustice framework 2 academic resistance and postcolonial theory in western universities indigeneity is often studied through the lens of postcolonialism which frequently classifies the arabisraeli conflict as a settlercolonial struggle the settlercolonial model because many early zionists came from europe they were historically categorized in academic literature as european settlers this framing often ignores the middle eastern mizrahi majority in israel and the geneticcultural continuity of the jewish people to the levant institutional bias many academic publishers have been hesitant to publish review slashfilm star trek starfleet academy is a weird show a funky one even while some old school trek fans will turn their nose up at the hijinks i just recall that virtually every mention of the academy in previous shows came with a wink and smirk suggesting the chaos everyone created and yes it also wants to appeal to the hardcore trekkies exploring the current status of the klingon empire a massive swing that connects with unexpected force betazed politics more interesting than youd think and the lingering mysteries of a certain season finale that trek fans still passionately discuss episode 5 is going to inspire some of the biggest online conversations in ages slashfilm star trek starfleet academy review this wonderful yaflavored series punches way above its weight class by jacob hall star trek starfleet academy is a weird show a funky one even in that it has to acknowledge the fact that this franchises puttogether captains diplomats and scientists all began as reckless cocky shy weird little folks attending college for the first time this is a star trek show where teen shenanigans frequently take center stage but also one that reminds us that with a little luck these kids are going to command entire fleets one day they just need the right education and when it works and it generally does starfleet academy is a joy starfleet academy is a show that operates on two separate but parallel levels up top we watch the schools educators and leaders as they induct the first starfleet academy class in over a century fallout from the events of star trek discovery and navigate a fraught perilous galaxy and the diplomatic pitfalls that await them at every turn down below we watch the schools students as they take classes join clubs bristle with sexual tension and generally deal with the anxiety of being a young hot humanalien with the weight of the universe on their shoulders the uptop stories are sweeping in scope the student stories more small and personal one is often the microcosm of the other even when they dont directly cross over while the galaxy deals with a sweeping event of grave importance the starfleet academy debate club argues about it its a terrific structure this kind of setup should be familiar to anyone who has enjoyed a story built around the magic school young adult trope before and yes there are times when starfleet academy could be described as star trek hogwarts thankfully the school campus is a place worth the investment a lavish piece of production design bustling with creatures and robots that can also literally lift off from its san francisco port and take field trips to strange new worlds in this way the series is a college soap opera that also well acts like a star trek show the young cast also makes a strong showing bringing all the angst youd expect from a series about young people living in a giant space school full of hot people but while the roguish caleb mir sandro rosta is presented as the shows central protagonist its the slightly more esoteric characters that bring the series to life karim dians queer pacifist klingon jayden kraag is an immediate standout honoring the legendary alien races past even as the show upends everything about their culture in a surprising and satisfying way kerrice brooks sam a photonic projection representing an isolated race of alien ai begins as comedy relief before becoming the catalyst for the shows most unexpected and moving moments but this cocktail is undeniably yaflavored and showrunners alex kurtzman and noga landau lean into it these kids are kids and they make mistakes and fall in love and struggle with homework and conduct ludicrous prank wars and in perhaps the funniest star trek sequence outside of the animated comedy series lower decks leave campus for a night of drinking and partying while some old school trek fans will turn their nose up at the hijinks i just recall that virtually every mention of the academy in previous shows came with a wink and smirk suggesting the chaos everyone created before they graduated its the right choice frankly i found myself delighted by the first six episodes of starfleet academy provided to critics i had a blast with the ridiculous comedic swings the intergalactic politics the often queer romantic subplots paul giamattis offthewall guest performance as a disgusting space pirate the fresh approaches to the trek universe and the frequent and i mean frequent easter eggs and callbacks to past alien species and events did you want the next generation skirtuniformformen back dont worry starfleet academy has your back i do recommend that skeptical trek fans give this one a chance and stick with it yes this series is a direct spinoff from the divisive star trek discovery but it takes that shows lemons and makes sweet lemonade the show gets better as it goes on especially in its thoughtful and joyous fourth episode and its hilarious canonrattling fifth entry controversial events like the burn have been given a new context acting as a metaphor for the hereandnow like the best trek has always done these kids have inherited a busted universe one the adults couldnt fix its up to them now and its easy to root for this crew rating 8 out of 10 link

evolve and adapt to various socioeconomic challenges many families are gravitating towards the suburbs seeking not just space and quiet but also a sense of community safety and enhanced quality of life this article delves into the factors contributing to the rising attraction of arkansas suburbs highlighting key areas amenities and lifestyle benefits that make these locales an excellent choice for families the heart of arkansas suburbs arkansass suburbs are a medley of rich culture growing economies and outdoor adventures cities like bentonville rogers and fayetteville have risen as beacons for families in search of a better worklife balance offering the charm of smalltown living alongside convenient access to urban amenities 1 demographic shifts and urban exoduses recent socioeconomic trends suggest a notable shift in demographics with families leaving bustling urban centers in favor of suburban serenity economic pressures fluctuating housing prices and the ongoing evolution of remote work are pivotal factors remote work the covid19 pandemic catalyzed a shift toward remote working environments families no longer tethered to their offices in larger cities can choose homes based on lifestyle preferences rather than commute times this flexibility allows for a greater selection of housing and a focus on quality of life cost of living the cost of living in many arkansas cities remains significantly lower than in metropolitan hubs families can enjoy larger homes and properties inspire better school systems and create a more balanced life without financial strain 2 community and familycentric amenities arkansas suburbs are becoming increasingly focused on familyfriendly amenities parks recreational facilities and community centers cater to both children and adults fostering a sense of belonging and community involvement parks and outdoor activities towns like bella vista and bryant offer numerous parks and recreational spaces activities such as hiking biking and community sports programs create opportunities for families to engage in wellness activities while building social connections with neighbors community centers many suburbs are enhancing local community centers to offer various programs classes and services supporting families these spaces host everything from art classes to fitness sessions serving as a hub for social engagement and personal development 3 educational opportunities a priority for families one of the most significant factors influencing family decisions on where to live is the quality of education available many arkansas suburbs have access to topnotch schools and educational programs highly rated schools suburbs like fayetteville and rogers are known for their wellregarded school districts which consistently receive high marks for educational performance strong focus on stem science technology engineering and mathematics education and extracurricular programs attract families who prioritize their childrens academic growth community involvement in education the growing trend of parent involvement in schools is prevalent within these suburbs many communities engage parents as active participants in school boards volunteer programs and fundraising efforts creating a welcoming environment for families 4 economic development and job opportunities as suburbs develop so do their job markets numerous businesses and industries are finding their homes in arkansas creating new job opportunities and boosting local economies corporate growth cities like bentonville home to walmarts headquarters have seen a surge in economic development this region is attracting large corporations tech startups and entrepreneurial ventures providing ample job opportunities for families support for local businesses the emphasis on supporting local businesses is also fostering a vibrant economy farmers markets craft fairs and local shops highlight the uniqueness of each suburb creating jobs and encouraging community investment 5 safety and security safety is a paramount concern for families and arkansas suburbs have outstanding reputations for low crime rates and community safety programs neighborhood watch programs many suburbs have active neighborhood watch programs fostering a sense of security among residents these initiatives allow families to feel comfortable and safe within their communities community policing effective community policing strategies have strengthened trust between residents and law enforcement making suburbs feel like safe havens for families of all backgrounds 6 cultural experiences and entertainment suburbs are no longer regarded as merely quiet retreats they have become vibrant centers of culture entertainment and social engagement arts and culture arkansas suburbs are becoming mini cultural hotspots with local art galleries theaters and music venues sprouting up for instance bentonville boasts the crystal bridges museum of american art providing families easy access to a rich blend of culture and education events and festivals seasonal festivals outdoor concerts and farmers markets are staples in many suburban areas ensuring that residents have numerous opportunities to engage in community life while enjoying local culture and entertainment 7 healthcare accessibility access to quality healthcare is another critical factor for families leaning towards suburban living many arkansas suburbs feature wellequipped medical facilities urgent care centers and specialty clinics health services suburbs like conway and north little rock are home to some of the states leading healthcare facilities ensuring families have prompt access to adequate medical care telehealth services which surged during the pandemic have further enhanced the accessibility of healthcare for residents 8 housing options and affordability the housing market in arkansas suburbs remains favorable for families with a variety of options to suit diverse needs suburban housing singlefamily homes with yards townhouses and even ecofriendly builds are all viable options for families the affordability of housing allows families to invest in their homes and communities more securely than in urban areas future development upcoming residential projects in suburbs ensure that they continue to cater to growing family populations offering modern amenities and wellplanned communities 9 access to nature and outdoor activities living in the suburbs provides families with the unique advantage of proximity to nature this connection to the great outdoors enhances quality of life and wellbeing natural parks and trails arkansas is known for its natural beauty and suburbs often serve as gateways to hiking trails lakes and nature preserves families are encouraged to explore the outdoors promoting both physical health and mental wellbeing community engagement in nature initiatives to preserve green spaces and protect local wildlife encourage families to get involved in environmental stewardship instilling values of conservation and community care 10 a familyfriendly lifestyle beyond the suburbs while the suburbs have much to offer families also appreciate nearby urban amenities access to theaters concert halls family attractions and dining experiences in nearby cities complements suburban life beautifully proximity to urban centers families living in suburbs enjoy straightforward commutes to urban amenities without the daily hassle of living directly in the city this unique combination enables them to enjoy the best of both worlds conclusion the rising appeal of arkansas suburbs for families can be attributed to various interwoven factors economic opportunities affordable housing quality education safety community involvement and access to a myriad of amenities as cities evolve and adapt postpandemic it is clear that arkansas suburbs are not just destinations for family relocation but thriving communities that embody growth connection and opportunity for a brighter tomorrow the allure of the suburbs in arkansas extends beyond mere geographyit reflects a profound shift in lifestyle priorities encapsulating a familyoriented ethos that resonates deeply with the needs of todays families as many choose to lay down roots in these vibrant communities the future of arkansas suburbs looks bright promising a fulfilling lifestyle full of possibilities future considerations as the dynamics of suburban living continue to evolve stakeholders must remain vigilant in meeting the changing needs of their communities sustainable planning investment in childcare services recreational spaces and public health initiatives will be pivotal in enhancing the attractiveness of arkansas suburbs for generations to come the journey of arkansass suburban transformation is just beginning and for families looking to build a bright future these communities may just be a perfect fit musthave baby furniture for your small nursery designing a nursery in a small space can seem tricky but with the right furniture choices you can create a cozy and functional area for you and your little one in this article we will explore the musthave furniture for a small nursery and tips that make the most of every square foot small nursery for small space having a small space is not the end of the world for nursery you can still set up a nursery that is functional and beautiful skip the nonessentials and start with a layout design consider these questions how much storage do you require what activities will you frequently engage in the nursery how can your furniture choices help maximize the available space once you have answers to these questions you can start building a list of essential furniture that meet your nursery needs essential furniture pieces at newborn nursery furniture we offer nursery solutions to simplify new parents life with a small nursery we suggest you have below items to maximum the use of your small space crib the crib is undoubtedly the centerpiece of any nursery when selecting a crib for a small space consider a mini crib or a compact model that adapts as your child grows convertible cribs which transform into toddler beds or daybeds can save space by eliminating the need for multiple pieces of furniture changing table a changing table is vital in a nursery but it can take up considerable real estate in a small space look for options that can double as storage solutions such as those with builtin shelves or drawers beneath some parents even opt for a dresser with a changing pad on top allowing for easy access to baby clothes and supplies nursing chair a comfortable nursing chair will save you from all the uneasiness during nursery some new moms love to nap on it during their late pregnancy and lot of parents state that having a nursery chair is one of the best decision they ever had but a nursery chair is not just for you it is also for feeding your newborn in the first few months for a small nursery consider an upholstered chair that fits snugly in a corner or a compact recliner additionally look for designs that blend stylishly with your home decor so you can keep using it later storage storage is crucial in any nursery especially in a small space invest in furniture that offers ample storage options bookshelves use wallmounted shelves to minimize floor space while displaying books and decor storage bins decorative storage bins can fit under cribs or be stackable use them to keep toys and supplies organized baskets stylish baskets can serve both decorative and practical purposes providing easy access to baby essentials changing pad if your nursery is tight on space consider a changing pad that can be laid atop any flat surface eliminating the need for a large changing table this innovative approach will allow you to quickly set up a safe changing area wherever you need it leveraging vertical space in a small space youll want to keep as much floor area clear as possible one way to achieve this is by utilizing vertical space effectively here are a few strategies wallmounted decor instead of cluttering shelves consider hanging decor items that align with your nursery theme overhead storage use ceiling hooks to hang storage bags or lightweight items like blankets and toys vertical dressers look for tall dressers or chests that provide more storage without taking up excessive floor space make your space cozy function is important but how about coziness here are ways to enhance your small nurserys comfort level warm color choose a light and airy color palette to help your small space feel larger soft pastels or neutral tones can create a serene environment perfect for your little ones sleep time you can use accent colors for playful touches or with decor items lighting in a small space lighting can set the mood opt for layered lighting options such as overhead fixtures combined with table lamps or wall sconces a dimmable light can create a calming atmosphere for nighttime feedings and diaper changes personal touches make the nursery a reflection of your family by adding personal touches hang family photos include handmade artwork or celebrate milestones with a growth chart these details transform your small space into a haven filled with love final thoughts designing a nursery in a small space doesnt have to be overwhelming by focusing on essential furniturelike a crib changing table and nursery chairyou can create a stylish and functional environment for your fitted a 1kb language model for the nes hi everyone i wanted to share a summer project that explores the question what if we had tried to implement language models on the nes in the 1980s my thesis was that we didnt lack the silicon for basic lms 40 years ago instead we just lacked the vision and the nes is capable of running tiny lm inference at game time so i wrote a bigram language model and turned it into a romhack for final fantasy and dragon warrior to generate procedural fantasy names for your characters but apart from the romhack the nes implementation itself was illuminating model weights 729 bytes uint8 quantized inference code 144 bytes footprint the entire thing is smaller than the tileset for a single black mage sprite yet it compresses a name space of roughly 18 million possibilities as we all know the 6502 doesnt have a hw multiplication let alone exponentials or floating points to get autoregressive token sampling working i had to avoid standard softmaxlogits i used inverse transform sampling using only sums and comparisons the logic looks something like this 1 pick a random byte as a target used ffs own rng lut 2 iterate through the model row for the current state 3 subtract the weight from the target 4 if the target drops below zero thats the next token turned out to work beautifully for generating believable fantasy names like dane deiona hannarqua at interactive runtimes code here id love to hear your thoughts on other modern concepts that could actually fit on the 6502 if we just got creative with the math

my so far gsoc 26 progress as a non technical background person for gsoc 2026 i decided to approach preparation differently than most students i am not from a computer science background i am currently pursuing bms which is generally positioned far away from classical software engineering or opensource security work however my interest in security and oss led me to owasp where i started learning practically by contributing to production code instead of studying theoretical material first after exploring a few owasp projects i narrowed my focus to blt because it sits at the intersection of security engineering cicd automation backend logic and contributor workflows rather than immediately writing a proposal i spent time understanding how maintainers operate what counts as signal in this ecosystem and what kind of work actually improves the platform this early research phase helped me identify that blt values correctness reliability and security improvements over cosmetic changes or superficial commits my contributions so far have been shaped by that insight i worked on peerreview workflow improvements that affected trust boundaries in github actions removed unsafe patterns such as verifyfalse in tls validation and addressed modellayer and formlayer inconsistencies that required database schema changes these contributions helped me understand production migration workflows django backend design validation layers and ci enforcement logic even as someone coming from a nontechnical academic track contributing to blt forced me to build a functional understanding of backend engineering and securitynot just as theory but as decisions that impact maintainability developer trust and product integrity what i found most interesting is how opensource reveals the real constraints of engineering correctness matters more than verbosity signal matters more than volume small changes can have outsized impact and communication with maintainers is as important as code this is very different from competitive engineering culture that focuses on algorithms or dsa in securityoriented oss projects the strongest contributions are often subtle precise and rooted in understanding how systems behave over time and at scale going forward my plan for gsoc is to develop a proposal around strengthening blts correctness validation and contributor experience this direction aligns both with the work i have already done and the longterm needs of the project ensuring schema consistency improving workflow security reducing regressions and making the platform easier for new contributors to trust and extend what makes this journey valuable for me is that it bridges business security and engineering blt exposes me to production tradeoffs maintainability vs complexity reliability vs delivery speed and developer experience vs enforcement i also want this to serve as a reference point for others coming from noncs backgrounds there is a misconception that gsoc is exclusive to students with formal computing degrees or years of coding experience in reality the differentiator is not background but the ability to think learn communicate and contribute to real systems my progression so far has been unconventional but it has also been intentional by combining research oss contributions and proposal planning early in the cycle i am building a stronger understanding of how gsoc works beyond the surfacelevel advice that circulates online gsoc 2026 is not guaranteed for meand that uncertainty is part of the process but the progress itself has already been meaningful i entered oss as a noncs student and found a space where security product thinking and engineering intersect if i continue in this direction my goal is not only to submit a strong proposal but to contribute work that benefits blt beyond the gsoc window
